summary: The root رَأَفَ (ra'afa) primarily signifies having intense, tender compassion and mercy. It denotes a profound and active pity, often leading to a desire to alleviate suffering.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: رَؤُفَ بِهِ , (AZ, T, S, M, O, K,) aor. رَأَُ; (AZ, T, S, O;) and رَأَفَ, (AZ, T, S, M, K,) aor. رَأََ; (AZ, T, S;) and رَئِفَ; (AZ, S, M, O, K;) inf. n. رَأْفَةٌ and رَآفَةٌ (AZ, T, S, M, O, K) and رَأَفٌ (AZ, S, K) and رَأْفٌ, (O,) the first and second being inf. ns. of رَؤُفَ, [or the first is of رَأَفَ,] and the third being inf. n.

(M, O, K) and and (K) and [which is the most common of all] and (T, S, M, O, K) are epithets from the verbs above: (T, S, M, K:) [the first from رَؤُفَ, like ضَخْمٌ from ضَخُمٌ; the second from رَأَفَ; and the third from رَئِفَ; signifying Exercising, or having, the affection termed رَأْفَة, i. e.
: see رَأْفٌ. الرَّؤُوفٌ is one of the epithets applied to God; meaning الرَّحِيمٌ [ The Merciful: or rather it has an intensive signification, i. e. The Very Merciful ]. (T.)
: see رَأْفٌ. [This art. is wanting in the copies of the Land TA to which I have had access.]

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
